findings.requirements: PerfDevOverlay's over-budget rows lose their destructive colour. Before, cn('text-overlay-foreground/70', priorityOver && 'text-destructive font-bold') resolved through tailwind-merge to 'text-destructive font-bold' — the overlay utility never reached the element, so the row rendered red. After, the hashed module class does not participate in conflict resolution, both classes reach the DOM, and the unlayered module rule outranks @layer utilities' .text-destructive. The row renders bold white. §4's D34 verdict for sites 1–11 ('no Mantine/shadcn ancestor CSS — WINNER (trivial)') looked only for ancestor CSS and missed a contest on the element itself. Fix must preserve the prior conditional composition for both budget rows and prove it for priorityOver=true and predictiveOver=true.
findings.evidence: docs/reviews/artifacts/2026-08-13-task748/cascade-repro.txt — fa-before color oklch(0.58 0.22 27), fa-after color oklab(1 0 0 / 0.7), measured rest and hover, 14/14 cells matched. Mechanism in docs/reviews/artifacts/2026-08-13-task748/twmerge-class-resolution.txt. Layer premise in docs/reviews/artifacts/2026-08-13-task748/emitted-module-chunk-ListingGallery.css (no @layer) and bundle-layer-and-offsets.txt (.text-destructive at braceDepth 1 inside @layer utilities). Sites: PerfDevOverlay.tsx:76 and :81.

findings.requirements: ListingGallery's photo-count Button changes hovered text colour. The ghost variant emits hover:text-foreground, which tailwind-merge kept on both sides; in @layer utilities it beats .text-overlay-foreground on specificity (0-2-0 vs 0-1-0), so before the change the migrated utility was a hover-state D34 LOSER. The unlayered module rule promotes it. This is a D34 loser under §3.4, not a latent contrast fix, and §10.3's rule is that a loser is left as a literal Tailwind class and reported. Per §3.4/§10.3 the disposition is an owner decision: leave the utility in place (AC1 and 695's exit condition then do not close) or authorise an exact-equivalence implementation with recorded before/after values. Not to be absorbed silently either way.

findings.requirements: The submitted comparator cannot observe F-A or F-B by construction, and §10.5 was substituted without being declared a deviation. §10.5 required capture before AND after; §6 uses a single build and compares each migrated element against a synthetic probe carrying the intended declaration text. That answers whether the new rule produces the intended colour, never whether the element renders what it rendered before — so any change caused by which classes reach the element is invisible. §6 further claims the method is stronger than a two-build live/live diff, which is false for this failure mode. Coverage is also 3 of 24 sites, and --plant corrupts the expected side rather than the subject. Replacement must capture a clean I0 worktree and the final tree, compare real elements, fail closed on missing/error/diff, plant against the after-side, and carry dedicated witnesses for the PerfDevOverlay budget rows and the mobile ListingGallery button in both rest and hover.
findings.evidence: docs/reviews/artifacts/2026-08-13-task748/executor-comparator/capture-and-compare.mjs lines 147-164 — the expected value is getComputedStyle of a probe whose cssText is built from `decl`, the intended declaration; line 155 shows --plant replacing that expected value with rgb(1, 2, 3). No pre-migration capture appears anywhere in the run. Contrast with the Task 691R closure, which captured a clean base worktree at 2ad067bc1 across 240 tuples in two real phases.
